_comment: Public GEO series with bacterial/viral acute-infection labels.
expected_counts come from published descriptions of these cohorts and act as a
CHECK on our own label parsing: if our parse disagrees, the parse is wrong until
proven otherwise. A null means we have not found a published count to check against,
so that cohort's labels stay marked unverified.

cohorts.note: Tsalik et al., acute respiratory illness, bacterial vs viral vs non-infectious
cohorts.source_of_expected: Tsalik et al., Sci Transl Med 2016;8:322ra11, PMID 26791949, doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.aad6873, Table 1 + text: 273 ill subjects = 70 bacterial, 115 viral, 88 non-infectious; Methods: two microarray batches with seven overlapping samples. Matches our parse only after exclude_samples (arrays 73/117/90 -> subjects 70/115/88). Checked by Claude (AI), not a human, 2026-10-21.

exclude_samples.reason: Re-run arrays of subjects already in the cohort (GEO 280 arrays, paper 273 subjects). sample_274..sample_280, batch 1; they carry exactly the label surplus over Table 1 (3 bacterial, 2 viral, 2 non-infectious). Identity INFERRED, not proven: GEO has no subject ids; cross-batch correlation supports it but the pairing is not clean (LABBOOK 2026-10-21). Excluded by the author's decision A, 21.10.2026; the 280-array result is kept as a README comparison row.

cohorts.note: Herberg et al., children, H1N1 influenza vs bacterial
cohorts.source_of_expected: GEO GSE42026 Series overall design (deposited by the authors of Herberg et al., J Infect Dis 2013;208:1664-8, PMID 23901082, doi:10.1093/infdis/jit348): after excluding co-infections, arrays analysed H1N1/09 n=19, RSV n=22, bacterial n=18, controls n=33 -> viral 41, bacterial 18. Cross-check: Tsalik et al. Sci Transl Med 2016 Table 1 lists GSE42026 as 59 subjects (18 + 41). The paper's own Results (25 H1N1 with 6 co-infected, 34 RSV with 11 co-infected) imply 23 RSV, one more than GEO's 22 arrays. Checked by Claude (AI), not a human, 2026-10-21.

cohorts.note: Suarez et al., respiratory tract infection, bacterial vs viral vs co-infection
cohorts.source_of_expected: Suarez et al., J Infect Dis 2015;212:213-22, PMID 25637350, doi:10.1093/infdis/jiv047, Methods: 158 samples [22 bacterial LRTI, 71 viral LRTI, 25 bacterial-viral coinfections, 40 healthy controls]

cohorts.note: Hu et al., paediatric febrile illness, viral vs bacterial. The 13 afebrile virus-positive children ('fever: no') are excluded, as in the paper's own viral-vs-bacterial test (the author's decision 19.10.2026).
cohorts.source_of_expected: Hu et al., PNAS 2013;110:12792-7, PMID 23858444, doi:10.1073/pnas.1302968110, Results first paragraph: 30 febrile children = 22 viral (8 HHV-6, 8 adenovirus, 6 enterovirus) + 8 bacterial

cohorts.note: Ramilo et al., paediatric acute infection, influenza vs bacterial pathogens. Run on three array platforms; we take GPL96 only, because the variants are the same patients and would otherwise be treated as independent cohorts.
cohorts.source_of_expected: Ramilo et al., Blood 2007;109:2066-77, PMID 17105821, doi:10.1182/blood-2006-02-002477, PMC1801073: Table 1 (set 1, training set) footnote: E coli n=29 + S aureus n=31 + S pneumoniae n=13 = 73 bacterial, influenza A n=18; Results: 'a total of 91 patients ... generated using Affymetrix U133A GeneChips' (= GPL96). CHECKED BY CLAUDE (AI), NOT BY A HUMAN: 2026-10-20 and re-read 2026-10-21 (the author's decision D2, 21.10.2026).

label_rules._comment: Applied to the lower-cased concatenation of a sample's characteristics. First matching class wins, so order matters: exclusions are checked before the two target classes.
